- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast dip by 0.5–1.0% to account for momentum lag.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model tends to overpredict further decline; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to reflect reversion.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 0.5–1.5% in early 2024; apply +0.5–1.0% upward bias for all forecasts unless sentiment strongly negative.
